blocks.explanation:
Yeh identity (hamesha sach rehne wali barabari) prove karni hai. Left side par do allied angles hain: \(180^{\circ} + \alpha\) aur \(90^{\circ} - \alpha\).
Diya kya hai? Left side. Prove kya karna hai? Ke yeh \(-\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\) ke barabar hai.
Plan: dono factors ko allied angle ke rules se chhota karenge, phir multiply. Har factor par teen sawal: multiple even hai ya odd, angle kis quadrant mein hai, aur sign kya hoga.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: L.H.S. \(= \sin(180^{\circ} + \alpha)\sin(90^{\circ} - \alpha)\).
Humein prove karna hai: L.H.S. \(= -\sin\alpha\cos\alpha\).
Tareeqa: \(\alpha\) ko ek chhota (acute) angle maan kar har factor par allied angle ka rule lagayenge. Rule har \(\alpha\) ke liye sach hai, magar acute maan lene se quadrant pehchanna aasaan ho jata hai.

Pehla factor chhota karein
\[\sin(180^{\circ} + \alpha) = -\sin\alpha\]
Kyun: \(180^{\circ}\) \(90^{\circ}\) ka even multiple (2 guna) hai, is liye sin sin hi rehta hai. \(180^{\circ} + \alpha\) quadrant III mein hai (\(180^{\circ}\) se aage thora sa), jahan sin negative hota hai. Is liye minus aaya.

Doosra factor chhota karein
\[\sin(90^{\circ} - \alpha) = \cos\alpha\]
Kyun: \(90^{\circ}\) odd multiple hai, is liye sin badal kar us ka co-ratio cos ban gaya. \(90^{\circ} - \alpha\) quadrant I mein hai jahan sab positive hain, is liye koi minus nahi. Yeh wohi complementary angle wala rule hai jo pichhli classes mein parha tha.

Dono ko multiply karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (-\sin\alpha)(\cos\alpha)\]
\[= -\sin\alpha\cos\alpha = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: Dono chhote kiye hue factors ko jor kar (multiply kar ke) bilkul right side wali expression mil gayi. Proof mukammal.

Tasdeeq: \(\alpha = 30^{\circ}\) rakh kar
\[\sin 210^{\circ}\sin 60^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{2} \cdot \tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{2}\]
\[-\sin 30^{\circ}\cos 30^{\circ} = -\tfrac{\sqrt{3}}{4} \;\checkmark\]
Kyun: Kisi ek angle par dono sides ki value barabar aana proof ka saboot nahi, lekin ghalti pakarne ka acha tareeqa hai. Dono taraf \(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{4}\) aaya.

blocks.explanation:
Is part mein koi variable nahi, sab angles numbers hain. Is liye har ratio ki exact value nikal kar rakhni hai.
Diya kya hai? Chaar ratios ka ek expression. Prove kya karna hai? Ke us ki value \(-\frac{1}{2}\) hai.
Plan: har ratio ko alag alag chhota karenge (chakkar hata kar, allied angle aur quadrant ka sign), phir multiply aur jama.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: L.H.S. \(= \sin 810^{\circ}\sin 630^{\circ} + \cos 135^{\circ}\sin 225^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: L.H.S. \(= -\frac{1}{2}\).
Tareeqa: Har angle se \(360^{\circ}\) ke chakkar hatayenge, phir allied angle aur quadrant ke sign se exact value nikalenge, aur aakhir mein sab ko jor denge. Ek ek ratio alag nikalna behtar hai, warna signs mein ghalti ho jati hai.

\(\sin 810^{\circ}\) nikalein
\[810^{\circ} = 2(360^{\circ}) + 90^{\circ}\]
\[\sin 810^{\circ} = \sin 90^{\circ} = 1\]
Kyun: Do chakkar \(720^{\circ}\), aur \(810 - 720 = 90\). \(\sin 90^{\circ} = 1\) yaad hona chahiye.

\(\sin 630^{\circ}\) nikalein
\[630^{\circ} = 360^{\circ} + 270^{\circ}\]
\[\sin 630^{\circ} = \sin 270^{\circ} = -1\]
Kyun: Ek chakkar hata kar \(270^{\circ}\) bacha. Unit circle par \(270^{\circ}\) seedha neeche wala point \((0, -1)\) hai, aur sin us point ka y-coordinate hota hai, yani \(-1\).

\(\cos 135^{\circ}\) aur \(\sin 225^{\circ}\) nikalein
\[\cos 135^{\circ} = \cos(180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ})\]
\[= -\cos 45^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
\[\sin 225^{\circ} = \sin(180^{\circ} + 45^{\circ})\]
\[= -\sin 45^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\]
Kyun: Dono mein \(180^{\circ}\) even multiple hai, is liye ratio nahi badla. \(135^{\circ}\) quadrant II mein hai jahan cos negative hai, aur \(225^{\circ}\) quadrant III mein hai jahan sin negative hai. Is liye dono ke saath minus.

Values rakh kar hal karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = (1)(-1)\]
\[\quad + \left(-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\left(-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\right)\]
\[= -1 + \tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[= -\tfrac{1}{2} = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: Pehla hissa \(1 \times (-1) = -1\). Doosre hisse mein do negative numbers ka product positive hota hai, aur \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} \times \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}} = \frac{1}{2}\). Phir \(-1 + \frac{1}{2} = -\frac{1}{2}\).
Dhyan dein: doosre hisse ko negative likh dena aam ghalti hai; minus into minus plus hota hai.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: left side ki value \(-\frac{1}{2}\) hai.

blocks.explanation:
Yeh bhi numbers wala sawal hai; chaar ratios ki exact values chahiye.
Diya kya hai? \(\tan 150^{\circ}\), \(\cot 330^{\circ}\), \(\sec 135^{\circ}\), \(\operatorname{cosec} 225^{\circ}\) wala expression. Prove kya karna hai? Ke us ki value \(-3\) hai.
Plan: har ratio ko allied angle aur quadrant ke sign se nikalenge, phir rakh kar hal karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: L.H.S. \(= \tan 150^{\circ}\cot 330^{\circ} - 2\sec 135^{\circ}\operatorname{cosec} 225^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: L.H.S. \(= -3\).
Tareeqa: \(180^{\circ}\) aur \(360^{\circ}\) wale allied angles (jin mein ratio nahi badalta) aur quadrant ka sign. Reciprocal ratios (sec, cosec, cot) ka sign wohi hota hai jo un ke asal ratio (cos, sin, tan) ka.

\(\tan 150^{\circ}\) aur \(\cot 330^{\circ}\) nikalein
\[\tan 150^{\circ} = \tan(180^{\circ} - 30^{\circ})\]
\[= -\tan 30^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\]
\[\cot 330^{\circ} = \cot(360^{\circ} - 30^{\circ})\]
\[= -\cot 30^{\circ} = -\sqrt{3}\]
Kyun: \(150^{\circ}\) quadrant II mein aur \(330^{\circ}\) quadrant IV mein hai; dono jagah tan (aur cot) negative hai. \(\tan 30^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\), aur cot us ka ulta \(\sqrt{3}\).

\(\sec 135^{\circ}\) aur \(\operatorname{cosec} 225^{\circ}\) nikalein
\[\sec 135^{\circ} = \sec(180^{\circ} - 45^{\circ})\]
\[= -\sec 45^{\circ} = -\sqrt{2}\]
\[\operatorname{cosec} 225^{\circ} = \operatorname{cosec}(180^{\circ} + 45^{\circ})\]
\[= -\operatorname{cosec} 45^{\circ} = -\sqrt{2}\]
Kyun: Sec ka sign cos jaisa: quadrant II mein negative. Cosec ka sign sin jaisa: quadrant III mein negative. \(\cos 45^{\circ} = \sin 45^{\circ} = \frac{1}{\sqrt{2}}\), is liye dono ke ulte \(\sqrt{2}\).

Values rakh kar hal karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = \left(-\tfrac{1}{\sqrt{3}}\right)(-\sqrt{3})\]
\[\quad - 2(-\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2})\]
\[= 1 - 2(2)\]
\[= 1 - 4 = -3 = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: Pehle hisse mein do negatives ka product positive: \(\frac{1}{\sqrt{3}} \times \sqrt{3} = 1\). Doosre hisse mein bhi \((-\sqrt{2})(-\sqrt{2}) = 2\), aur us se pehle \(-2\) hai, is liye \(-4\).
Dhyan dein: beech wala minus sign (\(- 2\sec\ldots\)) alag hai; usay ratios ke apne signs ke saath mila kar ghalat na karein.
blocks.final_answer: Saabit ho gaya: left side ki value \(-3\) hai.

blocks.explanation:
Is part mein chaaron angles \(180^{\circ}\) aur \(270^{\circ}\) ke darmiyan hain, yani sab quadrant III mein.
Diya kya hai? Chaar ratios ka jama. Prove kya karna hai? Ke yeh jama 1 hai.
Plan: har angle ko \(180^{\circ} + \theta\) likhenge, quadrant III ka sign lagayenge (wahan sirf tan aur cot positive), phir jama karenge.
steps:
Diya gaya hai: L.H.S. \(= \sin 210^{\circ} + \cos 240^{\circ} + \tan 225^{\circ} + \cot 225^{\circ}\).
Humein prove karna hai: L.H.S. \(= 1\).
Tareeqa: Har angle \(180^{\circ} + \theta\) hai. \(180^{\circ}\) even multiple hai, is liye koi ratio nahi badlega; sirf sign quadrant III se aayega.

Har ratio chhota karein
\[\sin 210^{\circ} = -\sin 30^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\cos 240^{\circ} = -\cos 60^{\circ} = -\tfrac{1}{2}\]
\[\tan 225^{\circ} = \tan 45^{\circ} = 1\]
\[\cot 225^{\circ} = \cot 45^{\circ} = 1\]
Kyun: \(210 = 180 + 30\), \(240 = 180 + 60\), \(225 = 180 + 45\). Quadrant III mein sin aur cos negative hain, is liye pehle do ke saath minus; tan aur cot positive hain, is liye aakhri do plus. Table se \(\sin 30^{\circ} = \cos 60^{\circ} = \frac{1}{2}\) aur \(\tan 45^{\circ} = 1\).

Jama karein
\[\text{L.H.S.} = -\tfrac{1}{2} - \tfrac{1}{2} + 1 + 1\]
\[= -1 + 2 = 1 = \text{R.H.S.}\]
Kyun: Do adhe milkar \(-1\) bante hain aur do ek milkar 2. \(-1 + 2 = 1\). Right side mil gaya.
